violated_invariant: Vault-owned USDC must not be swapped at an attacker-chosen pool price; swaps need a minimum-out bound and a trusted caller.
rationale: The PoC flash-borrows ~14M USDC from Morpho, dumps it into the USDC/WETH V3 pool to skew the price, then calls the vault's swapToWETH(100k USDC) directly from the attack contract and back-runs the pool to keep the difference. That only works if swapToWETH is callable by anyone and swaps at spot with no slippage bound, which matches the 'slippage' post-mortem title. The vault (0x6a06...) has no recovered source, so the function name comes from the PoC interface; Morpho, DexRouter, TokenApprove and the pool are tooling, not the defect.

violated_invariant: A signed VaultAuth must commit to every SwapInfo field (fromToken, toToken, amount, aggregator), not just the calldata bytes.
rationale: _validateAuthorization hashes only keccak256(swap.data) for each compound swap, so fromToken, toToken, amount and aggregator can be swapped out under a valid signature. executeSwap then calls forceApprove(fromToken, aggregator, amount) on the strategy, and the PoC sets fromToken to the gauge token, aggregator to its helper and amount to uint256.max, then pulls the strategy's balance with transferFrom. 0x5f0a... looks like the shared implementation behind the vault proxies (0x9c24/0x51b9/0x1d85, which have no source); the defect lives in this code. The PoC whitelists its own test signer, which stands in for the reused real signatures. No Slither finding describes the missing field coverage.

violated_invariant: The router may only pull tokens from a payer who started the current operation; standing ERC-20 approvals must not be spendable by third parties.
rationale: The PoC replaces the router's code with vm.etch, so it shows only the result: inside Core's lock/pay callbacks, WBTC is transferFrom'd out of a victim who had approved the router, 0.2 WBTC per lock, 85 times. Public write-ups say the router's payment callback never checked that the named payer started or agreed to the operation. The router (0x8ccb...) has no recovered source, so the defect can only be marked at contract level; Ekubo Core (0xe0e0...) is just the settlement layer, and none of its Slither findings apply. input_validation would also be a reasonable label.

violated_invariant: Every withdrawal paid by the rollup must be bound to public inputs that the verified proof actually constrains; total withdrawals must not exceed deposits.
rationale: Anyone can call escapeHatch while the block window is open. The PoC proofs encode rollupSize = 0, which validateMerkleRoots turns into numTxs = 1, and the verifier is called with rollupSize 0. processDepositsAndWithdrawals then pays publicOutput to an address with no deposit, draining all the ETH, DAI and renBTC. Reports blame a public-input binding gap between the processor and the TurboVerifier (0x48cb..., not in candidates, no source), so the exact defect line, and whether it sits in the processor or the verifier, is unconfirmed. The arbitrary-send and reentrancy findings on withdraw only describe the payout path.

violated_invariant: Calls the factory makes to the PositionManager as itself must be restricted to the intended pool-initialize and mint actions.
rationale: launch() is permissionless and passes caller-supplied initCalldata and modifyCalldata unchanged into PositionManager.multicall, with the factory as msg.sender. The PoC passes setApprovalForAll(attacker, true) as modifyCalldata, then burns the 7 LP NFTs the factory holds and takes both tokens. The PoolManager (0x0000...4444), which DHL lists as a victim, holds no defect, and Slither's arbitrary-send-eth on launch is about the dust refund, not this.

violated_invariant: A live contract registry's initializer must not be re-runnable, so only the legitimate manager can change the logic that item adapters delegatecall into.
rationale: The PoC calls initialize(1) and then acceptManager() on both registries with no privilege, becomes manager, and uses updateContract to make the adapter clones delegatecall its own transfer code. It then moves 54 items out of holders and melts them for 5.23M ENJ. Neither registry has recovered source; the only candidate with source is the ENJ token, which is not at fault. So the names here come from the PoC interface. The CSV victim_addresses is empty and should list the registries.

violated_invariant: A transfer of amount X must move exactly X token units; an amount that also parses as an NFT id must not move a whole 1e18 unit.
rationale: O404.transfer and transferFrom treat any valueOrId <= maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an NFT id and move a full units (1e18) of ERC-20 with it. The PoC uses V3 flash plus id-path repayment so the pool owns the low ids, then runs exact-output swaps of `id` wei, where the pool's transfer pays out 1e18 per ~2 wei of WETH. The defect is in the token (0xd5c0...), not in the pool or the Balancer Vault that DHL lists as victims; the Vault only supplies the flash loan. Slither's erc721-interface hits are about return types, not this.

violated_invariant: Interest for an idle gap must accrue once at the rate in force during the gap, not again on every action in the block at a utilization the caller just set.
rationale: _checkFirstAction stores the full idle block gap (264,059 blocks) and freezes actionEXR on the block's first action. Per the PoC, getInterestAmount then applies that whole gap on every later same-block action at the current SIR, which comes from deposit and borrow totals the attacker sets with a Morpho flash loan. UsdtHandlerProxy (0x808c...) only delegatecalls into TokenHandler, so it is not the defect; the interest model (0x29ec...) is not among the candidates and its code is cited from the PoC header. No Slither finding covers this accrual logic.
